producer: Phase 7.1 audit — orders / customers / finances. No code change, no canon decision (7.2 designs the types as [PROPOSITION]).

Every representation is 'observed' (a real payload was read) or 'schema' (the field set was validated against the platform's schema but no row exists on the connected source).

concepts.label: Identité de commande et numérotation (séquence, préfixe, trous)

woocommerce.orders.rest.v1.carrier: order.id (post id) = order.number (string) by default; order_key (wc_order_…); sequential-numbering plugins write _order_number / _order_number_formatted in meta_data
woocommerce.orders.rest.v1.numbering: post-id based: gaps are NORMAL (any post consumes an id); NOT contiguous; import via REST POST /orders assigns a new id — the source number cannot be forced
woocommerce.orders.rest.v1.invoice: no invoice entity in core (PDF-invoice plugins own the legal sequence)

shopify.orders.admin-graphql.v1.carrier: Order.name ("#1001"), Order.number (int, deprecated legacyResourceId also), confirmationNumber; shop.orderNumberFormatPrefix "#" / Suffix ""
shopify.orders.admin-graphql.v1.numbering: sequential per shop starting 1001; prefix/suffix editable in settings; NO gap-free guarantee is documented; orderCreate (API) can set `name`… only through the Orders API with write_orders + `sourceIdentifier` — never through the CSV (Shopify has NO order CSV import)

shopware.orders.admin-api.v1.carrier: order.orderNumber from the `order` number range (pattern {n}, start 10000, global) — observed ranges: order {n}/10000, document_invoice {n}/1000, document_storno {n}/1000, document_delivery_note {n}/1000, document_credit_note {n}/1000, customer {n}/10000, product SW{n}/10000
shopware.orders.admin-api.v1.numbering: NumberRangeValueGenerator: reserved on order placement, gap-free within a range unless preview/reservation is used; invoice numbers are a SEPARATE range on the document entity (config.documentNumber) — legal sequence lives on documents, not orders; Admin API POST /order accepts an explicit orderNumber (sync API) → a migration MAY pin the source number as orderNumber, which then collides with the range — must be reported (7.4)
shopware.orders.admin-api.v1.invoice: document entity (type invoice / storno / credit_note), documentNumber from its own range; 0 documents on the test instance

prestashop.orders.webservice.v9.carrier: orders.id (id_order, sequential auto-increment) + orders.reference (9-char alphanumeric, e.g. XKBKNABJK, used with the customer) + invoice_number / delivery_number (0 until the state with invoice=1 is reached)
prestashop.orders.webservice.v9.numbering: id_order is the auto-increment (gaps possible after deletions — PrestaShop does not delete orders in the BO); invoice_number is a per-shop sequence: PS_INVOICE_START_NUMBER (config, observed absent = 0), PS_INVOICE_PREFIX "#IN" (multilingual), PS_INVOICE_USE_YEAR / PS_INVOICE_YEAR_POS / PS_INVOICE_RESET, PS_DELIVERY_PREFIX "#DE", PS_DELIVERY_NUMBER 1; the invoice sequence is the LEGAL one (gap-free by construction: assigned only when an order_state with invoice=1 is reached); the Webservice POST /orders lets the caller set reference and id — pinning ids re-creates the gap problem on the target
prestashop.orders.webservice.v9.invoice: order_invoices resource (number, total_*, date_add) — 401 until the permission is granted (done locally), 0 rows because the demo orders are not validated

bigcommerce.orders.api.v2v3.carrier: order.id (int, sequential: 100, 101 observed on a fresh trial store); no prefix; custom_status; external_id / external_source for imported orders
bigcommerce.orders.api.v2v3.numbering: the id IS the order number; the starting number is a control-panel setting (not exposed by the API); POST /v2/orders assigns the next id — the source id can be kept only in external_id / staff_notes

wix.orders.ecom.v1.carrier: order.id (uuid) + order.number ("10001" observed — sequential from 10000), imported (bool), isInternalOrderCreate, createdBy
wix.orders.ecom.v1.numbering: sequential from 10000 per site; the Orders API import (ecom/v1/orders — createOrder with `imported: true`) keeps the PLATFORM sequence; the source number is not a settable field
wix.orders.ecom.v1.invoice: invoices are a separate Wix app (Invoices API) with their own numbering

gapVsCanon: CanonOrder.number is a bare string; no notion of 'source reference (immutable)' vs 'target sequence (generated)'; no invoice number, no reference vs display distinction (PrestaShop has THREE: id, reference, invoice_number).
concepts.handling: 7.4: CanonOrder keeps sourceNumber (immutable), sourceReference?, sourceInvoiceNumber?; the target sequence is never written by the converter; per-target report of collisions (a target that ACCEPTS a caller number — Shopware orderNumber, PrestaShop reference/id — is flagged, never used silently).
openQuestions: Shopify: is Order.name unique per shop or per location? (Shopify documents it as unique per shop.)

gapVsCanon: CanonLineItem {name, sku, quantity, price} — no product/variant source refs, no option values, no per-line tax/discount, no identifiers.

concepts.label: Ce qui est exportable / importable par plateforme (fichier vs API)

woocommerce.orders.rest.v1.export: REST GET /wc/v3/orders, /customers (observed); admin CSV export needs a plugin (core exports products only)
woocommerce.orders.rest.v1.import: REST POST /orders (id assigned, status/date settable, `set_paid`), POST /customers (password optional; role); core CSV import: products only. Orders can be created with a past date_created and `created_via`
woocommerce.orders.rest.v1.constraints: order number cannot be forced (post id); customer email must be unique

shopify.orders.admin-graphql.v1.export: GraphQL orders / customers (+ bulkOperationRunQuery for volume); admin CSV export of orders and customers exists (orders CSV is export-only)
shopify.orders.admin-graphql.v1.import: orderCreate (GraphQL, write_orders — sets financial status, processedAt, sourceName; `name` cannot be set on Shopify, only sourceIdentifier), customerCreate (+ emailMarketingConsent input with consentUpdatedAt — the API LETS a migration claim consent: must never be used to assert it); customers CSV import exists (accepts 'Accepts Email Marketing' = yes|no — same risk); NO orders CSV import
shopify.orders.admin-graphql.v1.constraints: order names are always generated; an imported order gets the next number

shopware.orders.admin-api.v1.export: Admin API /api/search/order, /customer, /newsletter-recipient, /document; admin export profiles (import/export module) for customers / orders (orders export-only by default)
shopware.orders.admin-api.v1.import: Admin API POST /order (explicit orderNumber allowed — 7.4 flags it), POST /customer (password required unless guest), POST /newsletter-recipient (status optIn — must never be set from source consent); import/export module imports customers, not orders
shopware.orders.admin-api.v1.constraints: number ranges are per entity; a pinned orderNumber bypasses the range

prestashop.orders.webservice.v9.export: Webservice orders / order_details / order_payments / order_invoices / customers / addresses / order_histories (observed after granting permissions); BO SQL manager / CSV export of orders and customers
prestashop.orders.webservice.v9.import: Webservice POST /customers (passwd required), POST /addresses, POST /carts then POST /orders (id_cart, module, payment, current_state — the invoice number is assigned by the state machine, never by the caller); BO CSV import: customers and addresses YES, orders NO
prestashop.orders.webservice.v9.constraints: order.reference / id settable through the Webservice → collision risk; invoice sequence is legal and only advances through states with invoice=1

bigcommerce.orders.api.v2v3.export: v2 orders (+ products, shipping_addresses, coupons), v3 transactions, v3 customers (+ addresses, consent, subscribers); control-panel CSV export of orders and customers
bigcommerce.orders.api.v2v3.import: v2 POST /orders (status_id, products, addresses, external_id/external_source; the id is assigned), v3 POST /customers (+ addresses, form_fields; `accepts_product_review_abandoned_cart_emails`), POST /customers/subscribers; CSV import of customers YES, orders NO
bigcommerce.orders.api.v2v3.constraints: the order id is the number; cannot be set

wix.orders.ecom.v1.import: ecom/v1/orders (createOrder with imported: true — number generated), contacts/v4 createContact (subscription status settable → must not be asserted), members require invitation; no CSV import of orders (contacts CSV import exists in the dashboard)
wix.orders.ecom.v1.constraints: order number generated; buyerInfo needs a contact

concepts.handling: The converter's targets for orders are API-shaped (no order CSV import exists on ANY of the six platforms); customers have CSV imports on Shopify / PrestaShop / BigCommerce / Wix — every one of them with a consent column that must be emitted as NOT subscribed (7.3).
